questions.explanation: Common pitfall: Triggering complex hover animations on touch-only mobile devices. Recommended fix: Guard pure hover flourish inside @media (hover: hover) so taps feel snappy.

questions.prompt: Which CSS property prevents a code block or card from splitting awkwardly across two printed pages?

page-lock: true

questions.prompt: When working with Print Stylesheets & Responsive Data Tables in CSS, which practice correctly prevents a common production bug?

Ignore Print Stylesheets & Responsive Data Tables constraints during runtime execution

questions.prompt: When a .card-host is 320px wide inside a 1440px desktop window, which background color applies to .card?

indigo
transparent

Only color: red
Both red and blue match
Neither matches

width and height
margin-top and padding
top and left

They work only on 3D WebGL canvases
They trigger layout reflow so siblings move out of the way

Ignore Individual Transform Properties & transform-origin constraints during runtime execution

backwards
persist

questions.prompt: When working with Keyframe Animations, Fill Modes & Timing Functions in CSS, which practice correctly prevents a common production bug?

Ignore Keyframe Animations, Fill Modes & Timing Functions constraints during runtime execution

questions.prompt: Which CSS at-rule lets you define the initial transition state when an element changes from display: none to visible?

@initial-frame
@enter-transition
@keyframes-start

questions.prompt: When working with Animating Entry from display: none with @starting-style in CSS, which practice correctly prevents a common production bug?

Ignore Animating Entry from display: none with @starting-style constraints during runtime execution
Replace Animating Entry from display: none with @starting-style with unvalidated global state mutations
questions.explanation: Common pitfall: Expecting a CSS transition to fire on display: none -> block without @starting-style. Recommended fix: Without @starting-style, browsers compute only the final style on the first frame, skipping the transition.

questions.prompt: After a 1s fade-in animation finishes with animation-fill-mode: none (default), what opacity does the element return to?

codeSnippet.code:

@keyframes show { to { opacity: 1; } }

1 (stays visible)
Browser keeps the last frame automatically

questions.prompt: Which step of the browser rendering pipeline is triggered when only opacity transitions from 0 to 1?
options: Composite only (skips Layout and Paint)
Layout, Paint, and Composite
Paint and Composite only
Full DOM re-parse

questions.prompt:
Given @layer base, utilities;, which declaration wins on

?

#hero.lead inside @layer base
Whichever has more classes
They throw a cascade error

questions.prompt: When working with Architecture with Cascade Layers (@layer) in CSS, which practice correctly prevents a common production bug?
options: Unlayered styles outrank every layer; keep your architecture consistently layered.

questions.prompt: Which selector selects a <label> element that contains a checked checkbox?

questions.prompt: Why is .btn { &__icon { width: 16px; } } invalid in native browser CSS nesting?

Native CSS nesting does not support double underscores in class names
The & symbol is forbidden in native CSS
Nested rules cannot contain width declarations

questions.prompt: In @scope (.article) to (.demo-box) { p { color: blue; } }, which paragraphs turn blue?

Only paragraphs inside .demo-box
Every paragraph on the page
Only direct children of .demo-box

questions.prompt: When working with Scoped Styles (@scope) & Donut Scoping in CSS, which practice correctly prevents a common production bug?

Ignore Scoped Styles (@scope) & Donut Scoping constraints during runtime execution

questions.explanation: Common pitfall: Assuming descendant selectors stop automatically at nested widgets. Recommended fix: Use @scope (.outer) to (.inner) when you need true donut scoping boundaries.

Every .form-row on the page
The next sibling after .form-row

Ignore CSS Containment & content-visibility: auto constraints during runtime execution
